'Same seat as last time?' Ramesh asked outside Lecture Hall 2, hand tight on his bag strap.
'Not today,' Jatin said. 'Last week I sat right next to you. On Monday, one seat away. Today I'll be in the back row.'
'The back row? That's miles.'
'It's twelve rows. You'll see my hand if you look.' Jatin held it up. 'I'll wave.'
Ramesh swallowed. 'What if my chest does the thing?'
'Then it does the thing, you breathe, and it passes. Like Monday. I was a seat away and you stayed the whole hour. That was you, not me.'
Ramesh nodded slowly and went in.
After the lecture he came out grinning. 'I only looked back twice.'
'Twice!' Jatin clapped him on the shoulder. 'Next week I'm getting coffee during the lecture.'

qa.q: How many rows back will Jatin sit today?
qa.a: Jatin will be in the back row, twelve rows back.

qa.q: How does Jatin feel when Ramesh comes out of the lecture?
qa.a: Jatin is delighted and proud of Ramesh, cheering 'Twice!' and clapping him on the shoulder.

qa.q: Why does Jatin keep moving farther away each time?
qa.a: Reducing the help step by step, and pointing out that staying the whole hour was Ramesh's own doing, lets Ramesh build confidence in himself rather than in Jatin.

qa.q: How does Ramesh seem to feel coming out of the lecture?
qa.a: He feels proud and a little surprised, pleased that he only needed to look back twice.

grounding: It shows a friend who first sits beside an anxious classmate and then moves farther back, praising the effort so confidence grows.

When Manjula signed up for the Saturday dance class, she made me promise to come. So in week one I danced too, badly, right beside her. She kept her eyes on me the whole hour, not on the teacher.
Week two, I stood at the back with my water bottle. She looked round a lot, but she finished.
Week three, I waited in the canteen downstairs. She came down flushed and said, 'I forgot you weren't there for, like, ten minutes.'
Each time I told her the same thing: 'You did that. I just stood around.' I meant it.
In week five she didn't ask me to come at all. She texted a video of the routine instead: 'Devika!! I got the turn!!'
I watched it three times. I was prouder than I expected.

qa.q: Where did Devika wait in week three?
qa.a: Devika waited in the canteen downstairs.

qa.q: What does Manjula's 'I forgot you weren't there for, like, ten minutes' suggest?
qa.a: It suggests her fear was easing and she was starting to feel safe in the class on her own.

qa.q: Which part of Devika's help built Manjula's own confidence?
qa.a: Stepping back a little each week while telling Manjula 'You did that' handed the credit to her, so she came to trust herself rather than her helper.

qa.q: How does Manjula probably feel when she sends the video in week five?
qa.a: She feels excited and proud, eager to share that she got the turn without needing Devika there.

grounding: It shows a friend going to an anxious person's class, then stepping farther back each week while praising the effort.

passage:
Lecturer's note, Economics 201, end of term
For the first month Jatin didn't attend my lectures at all; his friend Nandini told me that crowded halls made him panic. In week five he appeared in the very back row, Nandini right beside him.
Over the following weeks I watched her quietly move. In week seven she sat one seat away. In week nine, two rows ahead, turning once to give him a thumbs-up. In week eleven she came in late on purpose, and he had already found his own seat near the middle.
After each class I heard her say something specific: "You stayed the whole hour." "You asked a question today." Never grand praise, only the effort.
Last Thursday Jatin came alone and answered a question in front of eighty students. Nandini was in the library. I'm recording this because it is the best example of support I have seen this year.

qa.q: Where did Nandini sit in week nine?
qa.a: Two rows ahead.

qa.q: What might Nandini have felt when turning to give the thumbs-up?
qa.a: She likely felt hopeful and proud, stepping back while still letting Jatin know she was there.

qa.q: Why did Nandini's gradual moving away help?
qa.a: Reducing her help step by step while praising his effort let Jatin build his own confidence.

qa.q: What might Jatin feel answering a question alone?
qa.a: He probably felt nervous but proud, realising he could manage the hall without Nandini beside him.

grounding: A lecturer watches a friend accompany an anxious student to class and sit farther away each week, praising effort as his confidence grows.

subtype: Stage 6: Facing it in small steps [Observer]
passage:
Monday
Went to the gym with Uma again. In week one I stood right next to her treadmill the whole time; she wouldn't go in otherwise. Today I did my own workout on the other side of the room and waved just once. She stayed forty minutes. Forty!
On the walk back I told her, "You did that whole session without me hovering." She went pink and said, "You were still there, though."
True. Next week I'll drop her at the door and go get juice across the road. The week after, maybe she goes alone and texts me afterwards.
It's hard not to rescue her. When she looked over at me today, I wanted to run and stand beside her. But she looked, took a breath and kept going. I think that's the whole point.
Anjali

qa.q: How long did Uma stay at the gym today?
qa.a: Forty minutes.

qa.q: What does Anjali feel when wanting to run over?
qa.a: Anjali feels protective and a little anxious, but holds back, trusting that stepping away helps Uma.

qa.q: What is Anjali's plan for the coming weeks, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Drop Uma at the door, then let her go alone and text afterwards, reducing help step by step while praising the effort.

qa.q: What might Uma feel when Anjali says she did it without hovering?
qa.a: Uma feels shy and proud, still leaning on the fact that Anjali was nearby.

grounding: A friend accompanies an anxious young woman to the gym and gradually steps back, praising each effort so her own confidence grows.

subtype: Stage 6: Facing it in small steps [Observer]
passage: In the small town of Karjat, the computer course met above the grain shop on Tuesdays and Fridays. The first Tuesday, Avni walked her friend Tanuja up the narrow stairs and sat right beside her, knee touching knee, because Tanuja's hands had been shaking since morning. Tanuja lasted the whole hour. On Friday, Avni sat two chairs away. Tanuja kept glancing over, and Avni just gave a small nod. The next Tuesday, Avni waited downstairs at the grain shop, chatting with the owner about onion prices. When Tanuja came down, flushed, she said, "I asked the teacher a question. Out loud." Avni grinned. "I heard nothing, I was downstairs. That was all you." Walking to the bus stand, Avni noticed Tanuja was talking fast and swinging her bag. Next week, Avni thought, maybe she wouldn't come at all, and that felt good.

qa.q: Where did Avni wait on the second Tuesday?
qa.a: Avni waited downstairs at the grain shop, chatting with the owner about onion prices.

qa.q: How does Avni feel as she sees Tanuja swinging her bag?
qa.a: Avni feels pleased and proud of Tanuja, and glad that she herself is becoming less needed.

qa.q: What makes Avni's way of helping work well?
qa.a: She steps back a little each time, sitting beside Tanuja, then two chairs away, then downstairs, and praises the effort, so the confidence becomes Tanuja's own.

qa.q: What is it like for Tanuja when she comes down flushed?
qa.a: Tanuja feels excited and proud, a little breathless, because she did something frightening mostly on her own.

grounding: Shows a friend accompanying an anxious person to a class and gradually stepping back while praising the effort, building the person's own confidence.
